name: Motor-Driven Cycle
description: A light motorcycle or motor scooter whose motor produces no more than 5 brake horsepower (3,750 W), plus every bicycle with a motor attached that isn't a motorized bicycle or an electric-assisted bicycle. An electric bicycle too fast or powerful to be an electric-assisted bicycle or a motorized bicycle lands here. Defined by Kansas Statutes Annotated §8-1439.

restrictions.rule: A motorcycle or motor scooter whose motor produces no more than 5 brake horsepower (3,750 W), or any bicycle with a motor attached
Excludes motorized bicycles (3.5 brake horsepower or less, automatic transmission, 30 mph or slower) and electric-assisted bicycles
A motorcycle under Kansas law, so titled and registered as one
Riders need a class M driver's license
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a motorcycle helmet, and the operator must wear shatterproof eye protection unless it has a windscreen at least 10 inches tall
Must carry motor vehicle liability insurance
Needs at least one headlamp; one whose headlamp can't reveal a person 300 feet ahead may not go faster than 35 mph
